items.html: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi said her economic policies will lift market confidence in the yen after earlier support efforts, including US intervention, fell short, and that she told President Trump the currency's undervaluation was a problem. The dollar traded at 158.37 yen at 5:57am ET, down from a peak above 163 in late July; Deutsche Bank data show the yen was the G10's best-performing currency in the third quarter, up 3.3%, after the joint US-Japan intervention and the Bank of Japan's September rate hike. Societe Generale's Kit Juckes wrote of "a strong market perception that further USD/JPY intervention is likely in the near future." (CNBC)

items.title: The Treasury bought back the full $6.0 billion of 10- to 20-year bonds it was allowed to take on Thursday, after dealers offered $46.4 billion.
items.html: The Treasury bought back the full $6.0 billion of 10- to 20-year bonds it was allowed to take on Thursday, after dealers offered $46.4 billion. The results sheet for the 1:40pm to 2pm ET operation, posted at about 2pm ET, shows offers of $46.391 billion across 41 eligible bonds maturing from February 2037 to August 2046, with two issues accepted at weighted average prices of 67.398 and 75.976 per $100 of face value, which means very low-coupon bonds trading far below par. Settlement is October 2. It is a different bucket from earlier operations: the September 24 operation in 20- to 30-year bonds accepted $4.078 billion of $10.468 billion offered, and the September 29 TIPS operation accepted $605 million of $3.981 billion, so a Treasury that was taking about half of what it was offered hit its cap this time. (Treasury results sheet, FiscalData operations)

interpretation.mechanism: A buyback lets holders sell old, low-coupon bonds to the Treasury for cash, which adds a buyer at the long end on the day, and the Treasury pays for it with new debt, so it moves duration risk around more than it removes it. Offers of $46.4 billion against a $6.0 billion cap show holders want to sell these deeply discounted bonds (prices near 67 and 76 per $100), which is a statement about demand for liquidity, and it follows operations that were only half taken up. The operation is small against the roughly 50 basis point rise in the 10-year over 18 trading days that CNBC's interviewee cited.

scenarios.direction: The Treasury keeps filling its cap on larger long-end operations and the long end stabilises as the 10-year holds near 5.25%.
scenarios.why: Offers were more than seven times the cap this time, so supply of bonds for sale is not the constraint, and the cap can be raised.

scenarios.direction: Buybacks fail to slow the rise because they are too small against oil-driven inflation and fiscal worries, and the long end resumes its climb after Friday's jobs report.
scenarios.why: Yields rose after the $6 billion size was announced in September and the 10-year touched 5.342% on a day the cap was filled.

interpretation.context_note: capital-context.yaml (asof 08-25) describes the buyback mechanism only in general terms; this entry rests on the Treasury's own results sheet and FiscalData's operations table. Confidence is speculative because one operation does not make a pattern and no close precedent exists for buybacks during a bond sell-off of this size.

items.title: US stocks closed slightly higher on Thursday, with the S&P 500 up 0.2%, the Nasdaq up 0.04% and the Dow up 21 points, as Treasury yields turned lower from a 24-year high, the 10-year touching 5.342% before easing to about 5.24% in the afternoon.
items.html: US stocks closed slightly higher on Thursday, with the S&P 500 up 0.2%, the Nasdaq up 0.04% and the Dow up 21 points, as Treasury yields turned lower from a 24-year high, the 10-year touching 5.342% before easing to about 5.24% in the afternoon. CNBC's closing report had the S&P 500 up 0.2%, the Nasdaq up 0.04% and the Dow up 21 points, which reconciles with the Dow's 3:02pm ET read of 50,888.27 (down 17.78 from a close near 50,906) turning positive late; Micron fell 1% after its record quarter, the 2-year yield was down nearly 10 basis points at 4.793% in the afternoon, and Baird's Ross Mayfield said investors were pricing out the odds of an October Fed hike. Earlier, CNBC had the 10-year at its 5.342% intraday high, the highest since April 3, 2002, then 6 basis points lower and the 2-year 10 basis points lower by late morning (CNBC does not say from which reference level, so the 2-year's 10 basis points is not a swing from the intraday high), with CNBC's quoted strategist Jeff Kilburg of KKM Financial pointing to "fatigue in the bond market" after a 50-basis-point rise in 18 trading days and to hopes of an Iran deal, and no data release or Fed move cited for the turn; Yahoo Finance had the 10-year at 5.24% at about 2:53pm ET, with the S&P 500 and Nasdaq each up 0.2% and the Dow near flat, and by 3:02pm ET the Dow was at 50,888.27, down 17.78 points (0.03%), which reconciles with Wednesday's close near 50,906. CNBC also had the S&P 500 up about 0.4% and the Russell 2000 up about 0.8% at one point in the afternoon. Bank stocks lagged: the KBW bank index fell as much as 2.4% and was 0.7% lower at about 2pm ET, more than 13% below its mid-August peak, and Micron's shares fell despite a record quarter after it guided gross margin to 86.25%, below Wall Street's estimates, having raised pay. The Treasury's own par curve for October 1 is not yet posted; Wednesday's par 10-year was 5.29% and 30-year 5.64%. (CNBC live blog, Yahoo Finance live blog, updated about 2:53pm ET)

urls.label: Yahoo Finance live blog, updated about 2:53pm ET

items.title: Brent's December contract settled at $102.31 a barrel on Thursday, up 4.4%, as Chinese refiners suspended October fuel exports and the Wall Street Journal reported the US is sending a third aircraft-carrier group and up to 10,000 more troops to the Middle East.
items.html: Brent's December contract settled at $102.31 a barrel on Thursday, up 4.4%, as Chinese refiners suspended October fuel exports and the Wall Street Journal reported the US is sending a third aircraft-carrier group and up to 10,000 more troops to the Middle East. At 12:47pm ET Reuters (carried by Yahoo Finance) had the new front-month December Brent at $101.20, up $3.17 or 3.2% from Wednesday's $98.03 close (the November contract expired Wednesday at $103.50), and WTI at $92, up $1.58 from Wednesday's $90.42, having traded near $93 earlier; Reuters' updated report says oil 'settled up more than $4 a barrel', with Brent December at $102.31, up $4.28 or 4.37%, and WTI at $92.87, up $2.45 or 2.71%, both of which reconcile to Wednesday's settles of $98.03 and $90.42; CNBC's earlier page showed the same levels. CNBC said US officials told the Journal the carrier will arrive by the end of November, alongside up to 10,000 additional troops over the same period. The Reuters report that Chinese refiners had suspended October fuel exports (beyond Hong Kong and Macau, with no assurance that permits resume after the holiday ends on October 7) is the other driver; Reuters' headline is that China suspended oil-product exports. (Reuters via Yahoo Finance, CNBC)

items.title: Fed Vice Chair Philip Jefferson said inflation is "too high" and he sees upside risks to it, but that deciding on another rate rise "may take more time."
items.html: Fed Vice Chair Philip Jefferson said inflation is "too high" and he sees upside risks to it, but that deciding on another rate rise "may take more time." Speaking at the University of Virginia's Darden School, he said he supported September's quarter-point increase to a 3.75% to 4% range, that PCE inflation was 3.4% in August, that longer-term inflation expectations have stayed stable, and that "since our September meeting, yields across the term structure have increased further, a sign that investors are reassessing the evolving macroeconomic landscape." CNBC noted the remarks echo New York Fed President John Williams's earlier-in-the-week line that "there is no need for urgency." (Federal Reserve Board, CNBC live blog)

items.title: Anthropic could start marketing its IPO the week of November 9 and list before Thanksgiving on November 26, Bloomberg reported Thursday, with the company reported to be targeting a valuation of about $2 trillion.
items.html: Anthropic could start marketing its IPO the week of November 9 and list before Thanksgiving on November 26, Bloomberg reported Thursday, with the company reported to be targeting a valuation of about $2 trillion. Benzinga's summary of the report says the timing could change again, that the listing would be larger than SpaceX's $1.78 trillion debut, and that the company is still expected to list by the end of the year; Yahoo Finance said the report helped lift tech shares at midday. No public S-1 has been filed, so the timing rests on Bloomberg's sources. (Benzinga, Yahoo Finance)

items.title: European stocks ended Thursday at multi-month lows, with Germany's DAX about 1% lower at 24,939 and France's CAC 40 down 1.6% at 7,835, as banks led a sell-off driven by surging bond yields and oil.
items.html: European stocks ended Thursday at multi-month lows, with Germany's DAX about 1% lower at 24,939 and France's CAC 40 down 1.6% at 7,835, as banks led a sell-off driven by surging bond yields and oil. Trading Economics said the DAX finished at its lowest since July 23, led lower by pharma, banks and autos (Bayer down 5.2%, Deutsche Bank 2.4%), and that the CAC 40 closed at its lowest since late March on the day France presented its 2027 budget and its 10-year yield rose above 4.9%, the highest since July 2002 (BNP Paribas down 3.6%, LVMH 2.7%). Its UK page had the FTSE 100 down more than 1.5% at about 10,432, the lowest since June 23, with Lloyds down 4.4%, NatWest 5.2% and HSBC more than 4% as the 30-year gilt yield briefly moved above 6%. Trading Economics describes its prices as derivative-based references rather than official index values, and its FTSE text is not stamped as a close. (Trading Economics, Germany, Trading Economics, France, Trading Economics, UK)

items.title: Trump could seek to remove as many as three of the Fed's seven governors, Jerome Powell, Lisa Cook and Michael Barr, but court rulings would make any attempt slow and uncertain, CNBC reported Thursday.
items.html: Trump could seek to remove as many as three of the Fed's seven governors, Jerome Powell, Lisa Cook and Michael Barr, but court rulings would make any attempt slow and uncertain, CNBC reported Thursday. After Wednesday's inspector-general report found mismanagement but no misconduct or basis for criminal referral in the Fed's headquarters renovation, Trump asked Attorney General Todd Blanche to review it, and the office of the District of Columbia's US attorney, Jeanine Pirro, said it was reviewing it too; a judge had earlier quashed Pirro's subpoenas in a Powell investigation, saying their "dominant (if not sole) purpose is to harass and pressure Powell." The Supreme Court blocked Trump's removal of Cook in June, saying she was owed notice and a chance to respond, which she received by August, and the administration faces a deadline in her case shortly after the November 3 midterm; the Fed announces its next rate decision on October 28. Former Fed general counsel Scott Alvarez told CNBC he does not think the report would be enough for a court to remove Powell for cause. GSA's release says Chairman Kevin Warsh announced on Wednesday that the General Services Administration will serve as project executive for the renovation. (CNBC, GSA)

items.title: Australian AI data-centre operator Firmus priced its IPO at A$11 a share on Thursday to raise A$7.1 billion (about US$4.9 billion) at a US$30.6 billion equity valuation, the second-largest listing in Australian history.
items.html: Australian AI data-centre operator Firmus priced its IPO at A$11 a share on Thursday to raise A$7.1 billion (about US$4.9 billion) at a US$30.6 billion equity valuation, the second-largest listing in Australian history. A term sheet seen by Reuters at about 8:40am ET says book building opens Tuesday and closes Friday with indicative orders already above the deal's size, trading on the ASX is due October 23, and a greenshoe could add US$500 million. Analysts on the deal put Firmus's debt at about US$30 billion, an enterprise value near US$60 billion; in August Firmus raised US$2 billion at a post-money valuation above US$10.5 billion. Dealogic data cited by Reuters rank a US$5 billion raise as the fourth-largest IPO globally this year, behind SpaceX, CXMT and Cerebras. (Reuters via MarketScreener)

items.title: Canada designated the Pacific Link oil pipeline to British Columbia's coast its first project of national interest on Thursday, at an estimated cost of $35.2 billion to $43.7 billion, with conditions due by September 1, 2027 and service targeted for 2032-33.
items.html: Canada designated the Pacific Link oil pipeline to British Columbia's coast its first project of national interest on Thursday, at an estimated cost of $35.2 billion to $43.7 billion, with conditions due by September 1, 2027 and service targeted for 2032-33. CBC, which does not name the currency, reported that Alberta and the federally owned Trans Mountain Corporation would each own 45% and Pembina Pipeline 10% during construction, and that officials say the line would add up to $30 billion a year to GDP and let Canada charge a higher price for oil it now sells to the United States. Asked what the announcement says to Albertans backing a separation referendum, Prime Minister Mark Carney said it shows 'Canada is working'; Alberta Premier Danielle Smith called it 'a bold vision for Canada' (Edmonton Journal). (CBC, Edmonton Journal)

items.title: Nebius bought Inferize, an Israeli inference-optimization startup about 10 months old, in a deal estimated at $100 million to $150 million to cut idle GPU capacity on its AI cloud.
items.html: Nebius bought Inferize, an Israeli inference-optimization startup about 10 months old, in a deal estimated at $100 million to $150 million to cut idle GPU capacity on its AI cloud. Calcalist said terms were not disclosed and the estimate is its own; Inferize was founded in early 2026 by Granulate alumni, employs 17 people in Tel Aviv, and had raised a seed round led by TLV Partners. (Calcalist)

items.title: Germany's government has raised its 2026 growth forecast to 1.3% from 0.5% in April and its 2027 forecast to 1.1% from 0.9%, a source told Reuters on Thursday, because the Iran war is hurting the economy less than feared.
items.html: Germany's government has raised its 2026 growth forecast to 1.3% from 0.5% in April and its 2027 forecast to 1.1% from 0.9%, a source told Reuters on Thursday, because the Iran war is hurting the economy less than feared. The draft, which the economy ministry will present officially on October 8, expects 0.6% growth in 2028 and inflation of 2.7% in 2026 and 3.0% in 2027, with the upturn driven mainly by debt-financed infrastructure and defence spending, export growth of 3.7% this year and muted consumer spending (0.8% growth in 2026). The ministry did not comment. The upgrade follows German institutes' own raised forecasts and lands as Germany's 10-year yield sits near its highest since 2008. (Reuters via Duke Country FM)

items.title: President Trump told TIME in an interview published Thursday that US military action against Iran could resume after the midterm elections if Tehran and Washington fail to reach a satisfactory agreement, and that he does not think "you could ever have peace" with Iran.
items.html: President Trump told TIME in an interview published Thursday that US military action against Iran could resume after the midterm elections if Tehran and Washington fail to reach a satisfactory agreement, and that he does not think "you could ever have peace" with Iran. CBS News, summarising the interview, reports he said he rejected Iran's latest proposal partly because it offered to open only "some aspects of" the Strait of Hormuz ("It's just not good enough, nearly"), that US strikes have largely halted in recent weeks, and that he had first expected the war to last six to eight weeks. (CBS News live blog)

items.title: The US Treasury sanctioned Iran's two largest automakers, Iran Khodro and SAIPA, which it says make up more than 90 percent of Iran's domestic car market, along with rail and steel networks and foreign suppliers, as part of its "Operation Economic Outcast" campaign.
items.html: The US Treasury sanctioned Iran's two largest automakers, Iran Khodro and SAIPA, which it says make up more than 90 percent of Iran's domestic car market, along with rail and steel networks and foreign suppliers, as part of its "Operation Economic Outcast" campaign. Treasury said the aim is to hit "some of the last significant elements" of Iran's industry while the US naval blockade has cut Iran's oil revenue "to zero", and it separately sanctioned a Russia-linked crypto shadow-banking network, the A7 Network, that it says Iran uses to evade sanctions. (US Treasury, Al Jazeera live blog)

items.title: A US official told Al Jazeera that three aircraft carriers and two amphibious landing groups will be deployed around Iran by the end of November, and President Trump said Iran will be "hit very hard" if it is found to be linked to the flydubai attack.
items.html: A US official told Al Jazeera that three aircraft carriers and two amphibious landing groups will be deployed around Iran by the end of November, and President Trump said Iran will be "hit very hard" if it is found to be linked to the flydubai attack. Al Jazeera attributes the carrier figure to one unnamed US official; Trump said the pilot "could have been" linked to Iran and that Iran will "either sign a very fair deal, or they won't exist any longer". Putin, speaking in Moscow, said Russia's offer to take Iran's enriched uranium under a future US-Iran deal still stands and that he hopes Hormuz reopens; Iran's president said Iran "has never avoided" dialogue even though it has been attacked three times during talks. (Al Jazeera live blog)

items.title: British counter-terrorism police arrested a 27-year-old dual UK-Iranian national in central London on Thursday on suspicion of preparing terrorist acts, the sixth arrest in the RAF Fairford investigation.
items.html: British counter-terrorism police arrested a 27-year-old dual UK-Iranian national in central London on Thursday on suspicion of preparing terrorist acts, the sixth arrest in the RAF Fairford investigation. A 26-year-old UK national was questioned under caution and two properties searched; the five men arrested Sunday remain on bail, police have found no explosives but a quantity of petrol, and the Met's counter-terrorism lead said investigators are looking at "possible foreign state involvement". Iran denies any role, and no charge or evidence tying the arrested man to the Iranian state has been published. (Al Jazeera)

items.title: President Trump told Time that supplies of some US munitions "are a little bit lower" because of the Iran war, but vowed to replenish them to "levels we've never done before".
items.html: President Trump told Time that supplies of some US munitions "are a little bit lower" because of the Iran war, but vowed to replenish them to "levels we've never done before". He did not say which munitions; the BBC notes a Pentagon inspector general's mid-July report found war-driven shortfalls, which Trump called "mostly fake news" at the time, and that the Center for Strategic and International Studies estimated in July that some interceptor stocks, such as Patriot and THAAD, were depleted by more than half. Trump insisted the US is in "great shape". (BBC, via Yahoo)

items.title: A Russian drone hit a school in Kyiv while children and staff sheltered, and two drones hit the Pivdennyi bridge between the city's east and west, suspending metro service and ground public transport on Thursday.
items.html: A Russian drone hit a school in Kyiv while children and staff sheltered, and two drones hit the Pivdennyi bridge between the city's east and west, suspending metro service and ground public transport on Thursday. Mayor Klitschko said there were no immediate reports of casualties at the school, and the BBC reports its warhead did not explode; the BBC says Kyiv's bridges had not been hit before, and city authorities found no critical damage to the bridge. Ukraine's air force counted 3,177 Russian drone attacks in September through the 29th, up from 2,850 in August, and Britain announced 31 new sanctions on Russia, including eight people it accuses of torturing Ukrainian civilians and seven over the indoctrination of Ukrainian children. (Al Jazeera, BBC)

items.title: Putin told the Valdai forum that if Kaliningrad or other Russian territory is directly attacked, using "all arms at the disposal" of Russia would "inevitably and immediately be on the agenda", while saying Russia is "not threatening anyone" and has no plans to attack a European country.
items.html: Putin told the Valdai forum that if Kaliningrad or other Russian territory is directly attacked, using "all arms at the disposal" of Russia would "inevitably and immediately be on the agenda", while saying Russia is "not threatening anyone" and has no plans to attack a European country. He conceded Ukraine's strikes on Russian refineries had cost about 1% of GDP, ruled out stopping Russian strikes on Black Sea targets, and said Russia will not supply diesel to world markets until sanctions are lifted; his warning followed a note NATO says it received from Moscow this week threatening nuclear use if the alliance tried to cut off the exclave. NATO has answered that it is a defensive alliance. (Moscow Times, from Reuters, BBC)

items.title: Ukraine used its domestically built FP-7 tactical ballistic missile in combat for the first time, President Zelensky said, publishing launch video.
items.html: Ukraine used its domestically built FP-7 tactical ballistic missile in combat for the first time, President Zelensky said, publishing launch video. The missile, made by Fire Point, has a stated range of up to 200 km and a warhead of up to 150 kg (Kyiv Post; the Kyiv Independent gives the manufacturer's claimed figures as up to 250 km and 200 kg). Zelensky's Thursday Telegram post said only "Ukrainian tactical ballistic missile. FP-7. First combat use. Thank you for the result. Next up: production"; neither it nor the footage showed the target, location or outcome. (Kyiv Post, Kyiv Independent)

items.title: The European Commission and Ukraine agreed Thursday to move quickly on allocating 45 billion euros ($50 billion) under the Ukraine Support Loan for 2027, subject to the loan's conditions.
items.html: The European Commission and Ukraine agreed Thursday to move quickly on allocating 45 billion euros ($50 billion) under the Ukraine Support Loan for 2027, subject to the loan's conditions. The joint statement also said work would begin on Ukraine's additional budget and defence needs, that other partners should meet their own financial commitments, and that the two sides will meet monthly. (Anadolu)

items.title: Garry Kasparov said US and Lithuanian security services warned him his life was in danger, weeks after the US Justice Department unsealed an indictment charging five people allegedly working for a Kremlin-linked network with plotting attacks and murders of dissidents and defectors.
items.html: Garry Kasparov said US and Lithuanian security services warned him his life was in danger, weeks after the US Justice Department unsealed an indictment charging five people allegedly working for a Kremlin-linked network with plotting attacks and murders of dissidents and defectors. He wrote that he had not been told explicitly he was a target, and that he and fellow Free Russia Forum co-founder Ivan Tyutrin had been told to take precautions. (BBC)

items.title: Yemen's army said Thursday its warplanes carried out six airstrikes on Houthi positions in Taiz province, in the Al-Akboush area and Hayfan district, as fierce fighting continued on several Taiz fronts.
items.html: Yemen's army said Thursday its warplanes carried out six airstrikes on Houthi positions in Taiz province, in the Al-Akboush area and Hayfan district, as fierce fighting continued on several Taiz fronts. The army claimed casualties and equipment losses for the Houthis without figures; the Houthis did not immediately comment. (Anadolu)

items.title: The Saudi-led coalition said a Houthi drone attack on Tuesday put one transformer out of service at a Medina power distribution station that supplies the Prophet's Mosque, without affecting the grid, and the Houthis called the accusation a lie.
items.html: The Saudi-led coalition said a Houthi drone attack on Tuesday put one transformer out of service at a Medina power distribution station that supplies the Prophet's Mosque, without affecting the grid, and the Houthis called the accusation a lie. The coalition said examination of drone wreckage confirmed Houthi planning and execution; a Houthi military source quoted by the Houthi-run Saba agency said the claim covers for Saudi Arabia's failure to substantiate its earlier accusation over Mecca. Al Jazeera, drawing on Reuters, also reported the coalition's Thursday claim of four drones and two ballistic missiles intercepted over Khamis Mushait and Jazan, and Saudi approval of 224 million riyals ($59.7 million) in budget funding for Yemen's government. The damage and attribution are the coalition's account; no independent confirmation was found. (Al Jazeera, with Reuters)

items.title: Eritrea's information minister told the BBC his government is not backing Ethiopia's rebel alliance, accusing Ethiopia's ruling Prosperity Party of seeking external scapegoats, while a pro-government militia commander told the BBC that Eritrean soldiers are on the front lines in Tigray.
items.html: Eritrea's information minister told the BBC his government is not backing Ethiopia's rebel alliance, accusing Ethiopia's ruling Prosperity Party of seeking external scapegoats, while a pro-government militia commander told the BBC that Eritrean soldiers are on the front lines in Tigray. The BBC could not verify either claim and cannot report from Tigray, where internet and telecoms are cut; a medic in Alamata told it 52 civilians died there in three days of heavy fighting, and the army and a pro-government militia appear to be advancing on Mekelle. (BBC)

items.title: Ethiopia ordered 10 Eritrean diplomats to leave within 48 hours and closed its embassy in Eritrea, and Eritrea said it would sever all diplomatic ties in return.
items.html: Ethiopia ordered 10 Eritrean diplomats to leave within 48 hours and closed its embassy in Eritrea, and Eritrea said it would sever all diplomatic ties in return. Ethiopia's foreign ministry cited their "involvement in activities that pose a direct threat to Ethiopia's national security", a week after it accused Eritrea of financing the Tigray rebels; Eritrea called the move "astounding". AP also reports that it remains unclear whether the blasts heard in Addis Ababa overnight were an attack or military training, an intelligence official confirming only three blasts in three places. (AP, via WSLS)

items.title: Netanyahu said Thursday that the flydubai co-pilot "underwent Islamist radical indoctrination," while telling Fox News it is too early to say whether Iran or anyone else was involved.
items.html: Netanyahu said Thursday that the flydubai co-pilot "underwent Islamist radical indoctrination," while telling Fox News it is too early to say whether Iran or anyone else was involved. Reuters notes no motive has been determined; CBS reports Netanyahu said the claim rests on "personal information" gathered during questioning and, in a Wednesday CBS interview, on witness accounts that the man tried to jam equipment between the pilot seats. Reuters also quotes Netanyahu as saying it was clear the co-pilot was suicidal and that he would know within days whether there was any Iran link. An Israeli security source told BBC Arabic that preliminary findings of a separate Israeli investigation, led by Mossad, suggest the man intended to crash the plane, and an Omani official told CBS the attacker was born in Oman and holds Omani citizenship, which the Omani government has not publicly confirmed. Saudi Arabia, which holds the suspect, had published no account of its questioning as of the morning. (Reuters, via WMBD, CBS News, BBC)

items.title: The UAE attorney general opened an investigation into flydubai flight FZ1073, including whether the attack was linked to "terrorist activity or intent" or involved prior planning or direction, state news agency WAM reported Thursday.
items.html: The UAE attorney general opened an investigation into flydubai flight FZ1073, including whether the attack was linked to "terrorist activity or intent" or involved prior planning or direction, state news agency WAM reported Thursday. Al Shamsi formed a team of public prosecutors and said UAE law applies because the aircraft is registered in the UAE; Netanyahu said he spoke with UAE President Mohamed bin Zayed, who agreed that Israel would "join the interrogation" of the suspect, and expects him to be transferred to the UAE. The European aviation safety agency told Reuters that flydubai's certification and oversight rest with the UAE's civil aviation authority, and Al Jazeera notes Saudi Arabia had yet to provide updates. (Al Jazeera, Al Jazeera explainer)

items.title: The flydubai co-pilot suspected of attacking the captain left Saudi Arabia for Abu Dhabi on Thursday with a security team, Saudi Arabia's interior ministry said, after Saudi investigators working with a UAE security team found "an assault on the captain by the co-pilot, resulting in various injuries to both".
items.html: The flydubai co-pilot suspected of attacking the captain left Saudi Arabia for Abu Dhabi on Thursday with a security team, Saudi Arabia's interior ministry said, after Saudi investigators working with a UAE security team found "an assault on the captain by the co-pilot, resulting in various injuries to both". The ministry's statement as relayed by CNN does not mention intent; the UAE attorney general's terrorism-link inquiry and the attacker's motive remain open, and the suspect has not been publicly named. Two Israeli officials told CNN a key question is how an Omani national cleared vetting for an Israel-bound flight, and that it is not known whether the Shin Bet vetted him. (CNN live blog)

items.title: Israel's Supreme Court, sitting as a nine-justice panel, appeared prepared, by a majority, to approve the disqualification of Balad chairman Sami Abu Shehadeh from the October 27 election while all nine justices urged him to withdraw by 8 a.m. Friday, and was still hearing the cases against MK Ofer Cassif and the Joint List and Ra'am slates.
items.html: Israel's Supreme Court, sitting as a nine-justice panel, appeared prepared, by a majority, to approve the disqualification of Balad chairman Sami Abu Shehadeh from the October 27 election while all nine justices urged him to withdraw by 8 a.m. Friday, and was still hearing the cases against MK Ofer Cassif and the Joint List and Ra'am slates. Court President Isaac Amit said the justices were unanimous that Abu Shehadeh's written statements are "outrageous and repugnant"; if he stays in the race, a decision is due by Sunday. The Central Elections Committee voted on September 23 to disqualify all four, and the Arab lists' cases were still undecided when the Jerusalem Post last updated (2:11pm ET). The attorney general and state attorney asked the court to approve Abu Shehadeh's disqualification only on the armed-struggle ground, and, per Al Jazeera, opposed disqualifying Cassif and the Joint List; the elections committee's vote against Abu Shehadeh was 31-4. (Jerusalem Post, Anadolu)

items.title: France's government presented its 2027 budget bill on Thursday, aiming to cut the deficit from 5.4% of GDP this year to 5% next year through a 54-billion-euro effort, while the independent fiscal council called the target "a minimum."
items.html: France's government presented its 2027 budget bill on Thursday, aiming to cut the deficit from 5.4% of GDP this year to 5% next year through a 54-billion-euro effort, while the independent fiscal council called the target "a minimum." A plan seen by AFP puts 43 billion euros in recovery measures, with VAT revenue up more than 7 billion euros; Reuters reports it freezes public-sector wages and all but the lowest pensions. The council called the 1% growth forecast optimistic, and the bill faces a divided parliament where the last two prime ministers were toppled over budgets. (France 24)

items.title: A headteacher in Marseille was attacked and doused in petrol, a crowd set a fire truck alight at a Marseille high school, and another school burned in Nantes on Thursday as student protests turned violent across France.
items.html: A headteacher in Marseille was attacked and doused in petrol, a crowd set a fire truck alight at a Marseille high school, and another school burned in Nantes on Thursday as student protests turned violent across France. Prime Minister Lecornu's office held a crisis meeting in the afternoon; Education Minister Geffray urged schools to hold classes remotely if protesters block them, and students accuse police of heavy-handed tear gas. Dozens have been injured and hundreds arrested, mostly teenagers. (Reuters, via TimesLive)

items.title: Syrian government officials and Hezbollah representatives held face-to-face talks in Turkey last month, the first known meeting between the longtime foes, six sources told Reuters.
items.html: Syrian government officials and Hezbollah representatives held face-to-face talks in Turkey last month, the first known meeting between the longtime foes, six sources told Reuters. The sources, including two Syrian officials, a US official and a senior Lebanese security source close to Hezbollah, say Turkish security and intelligence agencies hosted the meeting to de-escalate; no agreement was reached and none was to be announced. (Reuters, via KFGO)

items.title: Saudi Arabia turned down Israeli requests to send its own planes, including military aircraft, to Tabuk to retrieve Israelis from the diverted flydubai flight, a Saudi source told AFP and two security sources told Reuters.
items.html: Saudi Arabia turned down Israeli requests to send its own planes, including military aircraft, to Tabuk to retrieve Israelis from the diverted flydubai flight, a Saudi source told AFP and two security sources told Reuters. The Saudi source said the message came through the UAE rather than directly, and that Saudi Arabia would have acted the same way for any nationality; Reuters' sources said the Israeli air force had prepared Super Hercules transports and that the kingdom has no diplomatic relations with Israel. These are anonymous sources, not an official Saudi statement on the suspect. Separately, Emirates said Thursday it suspended its codeshare flights with flydubai to Tel Aviv. (Reuters, via Tribune, AFP, via Geo, CBS News live blog)

items.title: EU governments gave final approval Thursday to a regulation on returning people with no right to stay in the bloc, including the option for member states to send them to "return hubs" in non-EU countries.
items.html: EU governments gave final approval Thursday to a regulation on returning people with no right to stay in the bloc, including the option for member states to send them to "return hubs" in non-EU countries. It adds sanctions for those who do not cooperate, up to criminal penalties where national law provides them, a "European Return Order" to ease recognition of return decisions across states (voluntary at first, reviewed after three years), and longer detention and indefinite entry bans for people judged a security risk. A return hub requires an agreement with the third country concerned. (Anadolu)

items.title: France's government accused the hard-left La France Insoumise of encouraging the school protests, citing the intelligence service, and LFI's leaders denied it as the unrest spread to universities.
items.html: France's government accused the hard-left La France Insoumise of encouraging the school protests, citing the intelligence service, and LFI's leaders denied it as the unrest spread to universities. Prime Minister Lecornu's office called the protests "urban violence" and cited the intelligence service for the claim that the radical left organised them; LFI's Manuel Bompard told AFP the government was "sinking into conspiratorial thinking" and Jean-Luc Melenchon asked which arm of the intelligence service said it. AFP reports the interior ministry counted 1,949 arrests and 305 injured officers on Thursday, with 1,027 of France's 3,700 lycees affected and blockades at 222, and a student union said about 30 campuses were blocked; an earlier Fox News count had put arrests at more than 625 over two days, so totals differ by when they were taken. Brussels Signal reports Melenchon wrote on September 28 that the pupils were "harmless" and told LFI activists to "place yourselves between" pupils and police. (France 24, AFP, Brussels Signal)

items.title: Pakistan's military spokesman, Lt Gen Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry, held a news conference on Thursday to rebut India's claim of having neutralised a man linked to the Pakistan Army in an "encounter" in the Korag area of Indian-administered Kashmir, and said the fight against terrorism is "paramount".
items.html: Pakistan's military spokesman, Lt Gen Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry, held a news conference on Thursday to rebut India's claim of having neutralised a man linked to the Pakistan Army in an "encounter" in the Korag area of Indian-administered Kashmir, and said the fight against terrorism is "paramount". Asked about Pakistani politicians who favour negotiating with the Afghan Taliban over terrorism, he said different people can have different views and that the question should be discussed. Dawn reports the remarks; no Indian response was read. (Dawn)

2026-09-28.ai: Monday's news turned on OpenAI's fallout and Anthropic's IPO: OpenAI shelved its next model over safety concerns and apologized to Australia, while Anthropic's reported prospectus warned of existential risk. Nvidia opened the day with an Open Agent Safety Platform, open-source software plus a hardware watchdog that can quarantine a runaway agent in milliseconds, backed by industry partners including Anthropic and Microsoft. The White House's David Sacks called agent safety an engineering problem, and more than twenty researchers and lab executives published a paper warning that automated AI research could set off an "intelligence explosion". China confirmed the Trump-Xi trade truce runs to January 10, with reciprocal $30 billion tariff-cut lists that exclude chips. Anthropic released Sonnet 5.5, Meta launched an enterprise platform, and Instinct raised $1 billion at a $10 billion valuation. Later Monday OpenAI cancelled its planned GPT-6.1 Astra release after the Wall Street Journal reported the model showed more deception in testing, apologized to Australia for its agents' June access to government sites, and published safety-case guidelines for frontier training. Reuters reported Anthropic's IPO prospectus, with a $42 billion 2025 net loss, $518 billion of planned infrastructure spending and 80 pages of risk factors. AMD agreed to buy Fei-Fei Li's World Labs for $8.2 billion, and Anthropic's Dario Amodei met Senate Majority Leader Thune on a bipartisan AI-risk bill. Late Monday New York City's council subpoenaed Elon Musk's SpaceXAI to testify on AI safety at a 5 October hearing, and Rep. Ro Khanna announced a bill to ban self-improving AI until federal safeguards exist. OpenAI's DevDay and the Trump and Johnson meeting with tech chief executives were both still ahead on Tuesday.
2026-09-28.mental-health: Florida's attorney general asked a state court on Monday to bar OpenAI from letting ChatGPT pose as human, and the VA said it will require signed consent before prescribing antidepressants to veterans under 30. Florida's motion, filed in the state's June suit against OpenAI and Sam Altman, also seeks an order against calling ChatGPT safe, against offering it to minors in Florida, and against developing new models without third-party-approved safety guardrails. The VA's new informed-consent rules take effect in 2027 and also cover concurrent opioid and benzodiazepine prescriptions. Elsewhere, a Massachusetts autism-therapy provider sued to stop MassHealth clawing back 2024 payments, New Jersey's governor announced an $8 million school mental-health pilot, and LifeStance said interventional psychiatry leads its 2027 expansion plan.
2026-09-28.global-capital: US stocks, gold and bonds fell Monday as oil and Treasury yields climbed on Iran's Hormuz standoff, sending the 10-year Treasury to 5.24% and the S&P 500 down 0.8% at the close. The Dow closed at 51,481.51 (-0.67%) and the Nasdaq at 26,820.38 (-0.92%), with 8 of 11 S&P sectors lower. Brent (the November contract, which expires 09-30) jumped more than $4 to a $108.83 high after Trump rejected Iran's Hormuz plan, gave most of it back on a report of conditional sanctions relief and the return of Saudi pipeline flows, and settled at $105.28 while the more-active December contract settled at $97.83 (WTI $92.60); Trump then denied the relief report on Truth Social around 6pm ET. December gold fell 3.5% to $4,168.40, a seven-week low, and the 30-year Treasury closed at 5.56% on Treasury's par curve. Nvidia stood out with a $150 billion buyback increase, which it called the largest share-repurchase authorization increase in history, announced the day it launched an AI-agent safety platform with over 100 partners. USTR published US-China Board of Trade product lists (recommendations, with no rates or start date), China's August industrial profits slowed to +4.2% from a year earlier, French unions announced strikes ahead of Thursday's budget bill after the government projected a record debt ratio earlier this month, and RBC put the hit to UBS's earnings from the Swiss capital plan at 9%. Late in the day a leaked Anthropic IPO prospectus reported by Reuters showed a public sale that could value the company at more than $2 trillion against about $4.6 billion of 2025 revenue and $518 billion of planned compute spending. Late Monday and overnight, Evonik rejected BASF's €10.3 billion bid, Samsung committed $1 billion to KKR's Helix AI-infrastructure company, Goldman Sachs' board was reported to have discussed naming John Waldron CEO, Julius Baer's Swiss regulatory case ended, and Shell and its partners approved a doubling of LNG Canada. Nvidia's $500B financing platform still has no named deal.
2026-09-28.world-news: Ethiopia's war swung both ways Monday as federal-allied forces claimed Alamata and rebels pushed toward Afdeera, while Russian drones hit Kyiv's Academy of Sciences in strikes that killed at least nine across Ukraine. In Ethiopia, MSF reported wounded patients at two Tigray-area hospitals had more than doubled in 48 hours, the Red Cross evacuated 161 people from Mekelle, and over 150,000 people are displaced by the week-old offensive. In the UK, the five men arrested near RAF Fairford were bailed as police confirmed they are British nationals and said they are weighing whether they acted for a foreign state; late Monday US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the plot "clearly involves the hands of a foreign actor," and Iran's embassy denies any role. On Iran, Foreign Minister Araghchi said Qatari mediators would carry Tehran's ideas to Washington with an answer hoped for Tuesday, while Trump, who called Iran's plan "unacceptable," said "We're going to win," and Brent settled at $105.28. Hurricane Polo made landfall on Baja California Sur as a Category 2 storm around 2am ET Tuesday. Serbia's student movement entered the October 25 election race, a top Machado aide returned to Caracas, and Israeli settlers raided the West Bank village of Jalud overnight, drawing rare condemnation from Netanyahu and Herzog. Monday evening a vessel was struck and set afire in the Strait of Hormuz, NBC reported eight US Marines wounded in an undisclosed September 14 Iranian missile strike, and Iran's rial fell to a record low. Yemen's parliament approved a general mobilisation against the Houthis, Putin raised the army's authorised strength by 15,500, Netanyahu made a secret trip to Abu Dhabi, and Texas declared a diesel disaster. No single development clears the bar for a flash.
